questions.question: Which of the following equations of motion is independent of the final velocity of a particle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**s = ut + 1/2 at²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The equation **s = ut + 1/2 at²** describes the **distance (s)** traveled by a particle under uniform acceleration (**a**), with an initial velocity (**u**) over a time interval (**t**).
 
• This equation is **independent of the final velocity (v)** of the particle. It only relies on the **initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and time (t)**.
 
• In contrast, other equations of motion, such as **v = u + at** or **v² - u² = 2as**, include the final velocity (**v**) explicitly.
 
• The absence of **final velocity** in the equation **s = ut + 1/2 at²** makes it unique and suitable for scenarios where the final velocity is unknown or irrelevant.
 
• This equation is derived from the fundamental principles of kinematics and serves as a practical tool for solving physics problems involving motion in a straight line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equations of Motion Overview:**

 
 
• 1st Equation: **v = u + at** – This relates the **final velocity (v)** to the **initial velocity (u)**, acceleration (**a**), and time (**t**).
 
• 2nd Equation: **s = ut + 1/2 at²** – This calculates the **displacement (s)** without involving the **final velocity (v)**.
 
• 3rd Equation: **v² - u² = 2as** – This directly relates the **final velocity (v)** and displacement (**s**), omitting the time factor.
 
 
 
• **Key Variables in Kinematics:**
 
 
• **u:** Initial velocity of the particle.
 
• **v:** Final velocity of the particle.
 
• **a:** Constant acceleration acting on the particle.
 
• **t:** Time interval during which motion occurs.
 
• **s:** Displacement or distance covered by the particle.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• Used in solving problems related to **free-fall**, projectiles, and vehicles under uniform acceleration.
 
• Widely used in fields like **physics, engineering, and mechanics**.
 
• Helps determine unknown variables like displacement, velocity, or acceleration in different motion scenarios.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics of the Equation s = ut + 1/2 at²:**
 
 
• Does not depend on the **final velocity (v)**.
 
• Requires knowledge of **initial velocity (u), acceleration (a),** and **time (t)**.
 
• Represents the motion of a particle in a straight line under constant acceleration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Final velocity is a critical variable in many kinematic equations, but **s = ut + 1/2 at²** remains independent of it.
 
• The equation is crucial in scenarios where the time of motion and initial velocity are known but the final velocity is either unknown or irrelevant.
 
• It demonstrates the **relationship between displacement** and other parameters in uniformly accelerated motion.
 
• Its derivation is based on basic calculus and the assumption of constant acceleration.

questions.question: Which of the following is a process in which absorbed substances from alimentary canal is transported to different organs where they are used to build complex substances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assimilation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assimilation** is the process in which absorbed substances from the alimentary canal are transported to different organs where they are used to build complex substances such as proteins, lipids, and carbohydrates.
 
• This process is vital for **cellular growth, repair, and energy production** in the human body.
 
• The absorbed nutrients, such as **amino acids, glucose, and fatty acids**, are distributed via the bloodstream to various tissues and organs.
 
• For example, **glucose** absorbed in the small intestine is transported to cells where it is utilized for energy production through cellular respiration.
 
• Assimilation is a part of the broader process of **nutrition**, encompassing ingestion, digestion, absorption, and excretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transpiration:**

 
 
• **Transpiration** refers to the process of water loss in the form of vapor from the aerial parts of plants, especially leaves, through stomata.
 
• This process is crucial for maintaining the **water movement** in plants and helps in nutrient transport, cooling, and maintaining turgor pressure.
 
• It is not related to the transportation of absorbed nutrients in humans, making it an incorrect option.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert sunlight into chemical energy stored in glucose.
 
• It involves the use of **carbon dioxide, water, and sunlight** to produce glucose and oxygen.
 
• This process is exclusive to autotrophic organisms and is unrelated to nutrient absorption or transportation in the human body.
 
 
 
• **Digestion:**
 
 
• **Digestion** is the process of breaking down complex food substances into simpler forms that can be absorbed by the body.
 
• It occurs in various stages in the alimentary canal, involving enzymes and mechanical actions.
 
• While digestion is essential for nutrient absorption, it is different from assimilation, which involves the utilization of absorbed nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Important Notes on Nutrition:**
 
 
• **Ingestion:** The process of consuming food and drink.
 
• **Absorption:** The transfer of digested nutrients into the bloodstream or lymphatic system via the walls of the small intestine.
 
• **Excretion:** The elimination of undigested and waste products from the body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Assimilation and Health:** Proper assimilation is crucial for maintaining overall health and well-being. Issues such as malabsorption syndromes can lead to deficiencies and health complications.
 
• **Role of Liver:** The liver plays a vital role in assimilation by metabolizing nutrients and producing proteins, bile, and other substances required by the body.
 
• **Energy Utilization:** Glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles for energy, while amino acids are used to synthesize proteins essential for cell repair and growth.
 
• **Applications in Medicine:** Understanding assimilation processes is crucial for diagnosing and treating conditions like diabetes, metabolic disorders, and malnutrition.

questions.question: A bullet of small mass and high velocity can penetrate a target deeper than a heavy stone thrown at the same speed because:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: It has less inertia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia:** Inertia is the property of an object that resists changes to its state of motion. An object with less mass has less inertia, meaning it requires less force to change its motion. A bullet with small mass has lower inertia compared to a heavy stone. This allows the bullet to penetrate deeper into the target as it does not slow down as quickly. *Hence, Option 4 is correct.*
 
• **High velocity:** The bullet is fired at a much higher velocity compared to a stone thrown by hand. The high velocity of the bullet generates significant kinetic energy, enabling it to penetrate deeper. However, the velocity does not relate to inertia directly. *Hence, this is partially related but does not justify Option 4.*
 
• **Mass and size:** The bullet’s small size and mass allow it to concentrate its force over a smaller area, thereby increasing penetration. While these factors contribute to penetration, the primary reason is its reduced inertia due to smaller mass. *Hence, Options 1, 2, and 3 are incorrect as they do not directly address inertia.*
 
• **Impact force:** The bullet’s reduced inertia enables it to sustain its high speed and impact force longer, unlike a heavy stone that slows down quickly upon hitting the target due to its higher inertia. *Hence, Option 4 is correct.*
 
• **Scientific explanation:** The penetration of a bullet is governed by physics principles such as momentum (mass x velocity) and energy transfer. The smaller mass of the bullet ensures less inertia, allowing it to efficiently transfer energy to the target without losing momentum quickly. *Hence, Option 4 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Inertia and Newton’s First Law:** Inertia is closely linked to **Newton’s First Law of Motion**, which states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. Objects with higher inertia resist changes to their motion more than objects with lower inertia.
 
• **Kinetic Energy:** The energy possessed by an object due to its motion is called kinetic energy. Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity (**KE = 1/2 mv²**), which explains why a high-speed bullet has significantly more energy than a heavy stone thrown at the same speed.
 
• **Momentum:** Momentum is the product of mass and velocity (**p = mv**). A bullet has a higher momentum due to its velocity, enabling it to penetrate deeper. However, inertia focuses more on the resistance to motion changes.
 
• **Factors influencing penetration:** Penetration depth depends on factors such as the bullet’s material, shape, velocity, mass, and the nature of the target material. The sharpness or smaller size of the bullet aids penetration but is secondary to inertia.
 
• **Applications:** The concept of reduced inertia is utilized in designing projectiles, bullets, and other high-speed objects for military, defense, and industrial applications. These objects are designed to maximize penetration and minimize resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton’s Laws:** The behavior of the bullet and stone can be explained using **Newton’s Laws of Motion**. Newton’s First Law is applicable to inertia, while Newton’s Second Law explains the force and acceleration relationship.
 
• **Force and Area:** The smaller size of the bullet concentrates the force over a smaller area, increasing pressure and penetration depth. Pressure is defined as **Force/Area**, and the reduction in area increases pressure.
 
• **Real-world examples:** Similar principles are applied in the design of industrial cutting tools, where small, sharp edges are used to concentrate force and reduce resistance.
 
• **Scientific advancements:** Research on ballistics and projectile motion continues to improve the understanding of penetration mechanics for applications such as defense, hunting, and engineering.
 
• **Practical implications:** The principle of reduced inertia is essential for designing efficient tools, weapons, and machinery that optimize energy transfer for specific tasks.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why hormonal contraceptive pills can have side effects?

options.text: They interfere with the body’s immune system.
They destroy the egg inside the ovary.
They disrupt the natural hormonal balance, affecting other physiological functions.
They prevent the sperm from reaching the egg mechanically.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They disrupt the natural hormonal balance, affecting other physiological functions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hormonal contraceptive pills** work by introducing synthetic hormones like estrogen and progestin into the body, which mimic natural hormones to prevent pregnancy.
 
• These synthetic hormones can **disrupt the body's natural hormonal balance**, affecting processes such as ovulation, menstrual cycles, and other physiological functions.
 
• By altering hormone levels, contraceptive pills can cause **side effects such as mood swings, nausea, headaches, weight changes, and changes in libido.**
 
• The hormonal disruption may also affect other systems, such as the **cardiovascular system**, increasing the risk of blood clots in some individuals.
 
• Hormonal contraceptives may affect natural hormone production over time, leading to potential long-term effects, such as irregular periods after discontinuation. ***Hence, the correct answer is: They disrupt the natural hormonal balance, affecting other physiological functions.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Hormonal Contraceptives:**

 
 
• Hormonal contraceptives work by **preventing ovulation**, thickening cervical mucus to block sperm entry, or altering the uterine lining to prevent implantation.
 
• The pills often contain a combination of **estrogen and progestin**, or only progestin, depending on the type.
 
 
 
• **Common Side Effects:**
 
 
• Common side effects include **spotting between periods, breast tenderness, nausea, and weight gain.**
 
• Long-term use may increase the risk of **hypertension, blood clots, or stroke** in individuals with predisposing factors.
 
 
 
• **Non-Hormonal Contraceptive Methods:**
 
 
• Non-hormonal methods such as **condoms, copper IUDs, or diaphragms** work mechanically or chemically without altering hormonal balance.
 
• These methods are preferred by individuals who want to avoid hormonal side effects or have contraindications for hormonal contraceptives.
 
 
 
• **Contraindications for Hormonal Contraceptives:**
 
 
• Hormonal contraceptives are contraindicated in individuals with a history of **blood clots, stroke, breast cancer, or uncontrolled hypertension.**
 
• They are also not recommended for smokers over the age of 35 due to increased cardiovascular risks.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The first oral contraceptive pill was approved by the **FDA in 1960**, revolutionizing reproductive health and family planning globally.
 
• Modern contraceptives are more refined, with lower doses of hormones to reduce side effects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: They interfere with the body’s immune system.**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect as hormonal contraceptives primarily affect the reproductive system and hormonal balance rather than directly interfering with the immune system.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: They destroy the egg inside the ovary.**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because hormonal contraceptives prevent ovulation rather than destroying eggs.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: They prevent the sperm from reaching the egg mechanically.**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because hormonal pills work chemically by altering hormones, not mechanically.
 
 
 
• **Global Statistics:**
 
 
• As per the **WHO**, approximately **214 million women** globally use hormonal contraceptives.
 
• Hormonal contraceptives are widely used due to their **high efficacy rates**, ranging from 91% to 99% when used correctly.

questions.question: The plant cell wall is primarily composed of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **primary component of plant cell walls** is **cellulose**, a complex carbohydrate and polysaccharide made up of long chains of glucose units.
 
• **Cellulose** provides structural support and rigidity to plant cells by forming microfibrils, which are strong, fibrous structures within the cell wall.
 
• **Cell walls** are unique to plant cells and some algae, and they play a critical role in maintaining cell shape, protecting against mechanical stress, and regulating water uptake.
 
• Unlike cellulose, **chitin** (Option 1) is a major structural component of fungal cell walls and the exoskeletons of arthropods, not plant cells. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **N-Acetyl glucosamine** (Option 2) is a derivative of glucose and is a monomer of chitin, which is unrelated to plant cell walls. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Suberin** (Option 4) is a waxy substance found in the cork of plants and acts as a barrier to water and pathogens but is not the primary structural component of cell walls. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Cellulose:**

 
 
• Cellulose is composed of **beta-glucose monomers** linked by **beta-1,4-glycosidic bonds**.
 
• These linear chains aggregate to form **microfibrils**, which provide tensile strength to the cell wall.
 
• It is considered the most abundant organic polymer on Earth.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Plant Cell Walls:**
 
 
• Plant cell walls provide **mechanical support** and maintain the cell's shape.
 
• They act as a barrier against **pathogens**, helping protect the cell from infections.
 
• Cell walls regulate **water intake** by preventing the cell from bursting due to excessive water absorption.
 
• They are involved in **cell-cell communication** and transport of nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Other Components of Plant Cell Walls:**
 
 
• In addition to cellulose, plant cell walls contain **hemicellulose**, **pectin**, and **lignin**.
 
• **Hemicellulose**: A polysaccharide that binds cellulose fibers together.
 
• **Pectin**: A gel-like substance that helps in adhesion between cell walls.
 
• **Lignin**: A polymer that adds rigidity and waterproofing to secondary cell walls.
 
 
 
• **Examples and Applications:**
 
 
• Cellulose is used in industries to produce **paper**, **textiles**, and **biofuels**.
 
• Dietary cellulose, known as **fiber**, is essential for human digestion as it aids in bowel movement.
 
• Cellulose derivatives like **cellulose acetate** are used in plastics and photographic films.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery of Cellulose:**

 
 
• Cellulose was first identified in **1838** by French chemist **Anselme Payen**.
 
• Its molecular structure was elucidated later with the advent of advanced techniques like X-ray crystallography.
 
 
 
• **Role in Bioenergy:**
 
 
• Cellulose is a key component in the production of **bioethanol**, a renewable energy source.
 
• Enzymes like **cellulase** are used to break down cellulose into fermentable sugars for biofuel production.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Cellulose is biodegradable and plays a role in the **carbon cycle**, as it is decomposed by microorganisms.
 
• Its industrial uses, such as in paper production, can have environmental consequences if not managed sustainably.

questions.question: What happens when a pendulum bob swings from its mean position to extreme position?

options.text: Both kinetic and potential energies increase
Potential energy decreases, kinetic energy increases
Potential energy increases, kinetic energy decreases

questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Potential energy increases, kinetic energy decreases**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • When the pendulum bob swings from its **mean position** (equilibrium point) to the **extreme position**, the **potential energy increases** because the height of the bob increases relative to the lowest point. At the extreme position, the pendulum has maximum potential energy. • As the pendulum moves away from the mean position, its **kinetic energy decreases**. This is because the speed of the pendulum reduces as it approaches the extreme position due to the conversion of kinetic energy into potential energy. • At the mean position, the pendulum has **maximum kinetic energy** and minimum potential energy, as it moves the fastest at this point. • At the extreme position, the pendulum comes to a momentary halt, thus having **zero kinetic energy** and maximum potential energy. • This energy transformation follows the principle of conservation of energy, where the **total mechanical energy** (sum of kinetic and potential energies) remains constant throughout the motion.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies an element that DOES NOT exist as a molecule in nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium** is a noble gas and exists as a **monoatomic element** in nature, not as a molecule. This is because noble gases have a complete outer electron shell, making them highly stable and unreactive.
 
• Unlike elements such as **Chlorine (Cl₂)**, **Hydrogen (H₂)**, and **Iodine (I₂)**, which form diatomic molecules in their natural state due to their need to achieve stability through covalent bonding, helium does not need to bond with other atoms.
 
• Chlorine, hydrogen, and iodine naturally form diatomic molecules because their atoms share electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration (the octet rule).
 
• Helium is part of Group 18 (the noble gases) in the periodic table and has only two electrons in its outer shell, which is the maximum capacity for the first energy level. This makes it inherently stable.
 
• Helium's inertness and stability are why it exists as single atoms in nature, unlike other elements listed in the question.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Noble Gases:**

 
 
• The noble gases include **helium (He)**, **neon (Ne)**, **argon (Ar)**, **krypton (Kr)**, **xenon (Xe)**, and **radon (Rn)**.
 
• They are characterized by their **complete valence electron shells**, which make them chemically inert and highly stable under normal conditions.
 
• Noble gases are often used in applications where reactivity needs to be minimized, such as helium in balloons or neon in lighting.
 
 
 
• **Diatomic Molecules:**
 
 
• Elements like **hydrogen (H₂)**, **chlorine (Cl₂)**, and **iodine (I₂)** naturally exist as diatomic molecules because they share electrons through covalent bonds to achieve a stable electronic configuration.
 
• The diatomic nature of these molecules ensures their stability and is a common feature among nonmetals in the periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Helium's Applications:**
 
 
• Helium is widely used in **cryogenics**, particularly in the cooling of superconducting magnets.
 
• It is also used in **scientific research** as an inert atmosphere for experiments and as a carrier gas in gas chromatography.
 
• Helium’s low density and non-flammable nature make it ideal for filling balloons and airships.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table Grouping:**
 
 
• The periodic table groups elements based on their chemical properties, and noble gases are placed in Group 18 due to their **inert nature**.
 
• In contrast, elements like chlorine and iodine belong to the halogens in Group 17, characterized by their high reactivity and tendency to form diatomic molecules.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Monoatomic vs. Diatomic Elements:**

 
 
• **Monoatomic:** Helium and other noble gases naturally exist as single atoms due to their stability.
 
• **Diatomic:** Nonmetal elements like hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine, and iodine form diatomic molecules to achieve stability through covalent bonding.
 
 
 
• **Helium Discovery:**
 
 
• Helium was first discovered in the **sun's spectrum** during a solar eclipse in **1868** by French astronomer **Jules Janssen** and English astronomer **Norman Lockyer**.
 
• The element is named after the Greek word **“Helios”**, meaning the sun.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity of Noble Gases:**
 
 
• Noble gases are generally unreactive due to their complete electron shells, but under extreme conditions, some (like xenon) can form compounds with highly electronegative elements like fluorine.

questions.question: A poultry farmer wants birds that consume less feed, tolerate high heat, and produce quality chicks. Which strategy should he follow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cross-breed exotic and local poultry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cross-breeding exotic and local poultry** combines the desirable traits of both breeds, leading to birds that are more efficient in feed consumption, heat tolerance, and productivity. This is particularly beneficial for adapting to regional climatic conditions and improving output.
 
• **Local poultry breeds** are naturally adapted to harsh environmental conditions, such as high temperatures. When crossbred with exotic breeds, the resulting offspring inherit heat tolerance from local breeds and high productivity traits from exotic breeds.
 
• **Feed efficiency:** Exotic breeds are often genetically selected for better feed conversion ratios, meaning they produce more output (e.g., eggs, meat) with less feed. Cross-breeding helps transfer this efficiency to the hybrid birds.
 
• **Quality chicks:** Crossbred birds often produce healthier and more robust chicks due to hybrid vigor, which enhances growth rate, disease resistance, and survival chances.
 
• This strategy is widely practiced in modern poultry farming and has been shown to improve the profitability and sustainability of poultry operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indigenous poultry breeds:**

 
 
• Examples include **Aseel, Kadaknath, and Chittagong**, which are known for their adaptability to local climates, disease resistance, and moderate productivity.
 
• These breeds are typically used for backyard farming and are popular for their flavorful meat and organic eggs.
 
 
 
• **Exotic poultry breeds:**
 
 
• Examples include **White Leghorn, Rhode Island Red, and Plymouth Rock**, which are known for their high egg and meat production.
 
• These breeds are commercially bred and perform well in controlled environments but may struggle in extreme climatic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of cross-breeding:**
 
 
• Hybrid birds exhibit **heterosis (hybrid vigor)**, which enhances growth, reproduction, and survival traits.
 
• Adaptability to local environmental conditions improves, reducing mortality rates and production losses.
 
• Higher productivity ensures better economic returns for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Other strategies in poultry farming:**
 
 
• **Feed birds twice a day:** This is a routine practice but does not directly address the farmer's need for heat tolerance, feed efficiency, or chick quality.
 
• **Shift to fish farming:** While this may diversify income, it does not solve the problem related to poultry farming needs.
 
• **Use only indigenous birds:** Although indigenous birds are heat-tolerant, they generally have lower productivity compared to crossbred or exotic breeds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hybrid vigor:** The phenomenon where crossbred offspring show superior traits compared to their parent breeds. This is crucial for enhancing productivity and survivability in poultry.
 
• **Feed conversion ratio (FCR):** A key metric in poultry farming that measures the efficiency with which birds convert feed into body mass (meat) or eggs.
 
• **Heat tolerance:** Local breeds have physiological and genetic traits that help them thrive in high-temperature regions, which can be passed on to hybrids.
 
• **Economic benefits:** Crossbreeding reduces feed costs, increases productivity, and improves the overall profitability of poultry farming operations.

questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is caused by a bacterium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gonorrhoea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gonorrhoea** is a sexually transmitted disease (STD) caused by the bacterium **Neisseria gonorrhoeae**.
 
• The bacterium infects the mucous membranes of the reproductive tract, including the cervix, uterus, and fallopian tubes in women, and the urethra in men and women.
 
• It is transmitted through sexual contact, including vaginal, oral, and anal sex, with an infected person.
 
• Symptoms in males may include a burning sensation during urination and discharge from the penis, while females may experience vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, or irregular bleeding. Some cases, however, may remain asymptomatic.
 
• Untreated gonorrhoea can lead to serious health complications such as pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) in women, infertility in both men and women, and an increased risk of HIV transmission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Typhoid:**

 
 
• Typhoid is a bacterial infection caused by **Salmonella typhi**.
 
• It is not sexually transmitted but is spread through contaminated food or water.
 
• Symptoms include high fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and constipation or diarrhea.
 
 
 
• **HIV-AIDS:**
 
 
• HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) causes AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome).
 
• It is a sexually transmitted infection (STI), but it is caused by a **virus**, not a bacterium.
 
• HIV weakens the immune system, making individuals more susceptible to infections and certain cancers.
 
 
 
• **Warts:**
 
 
• Warts, particularly genital warts, are caused by certain strains of the **Human Papillomavirus (HPV)**.
 
• HPV is a sexually transmitted virus, but it is not bacterial in origin.
 
• Prevention includes vaccination and safe sexual practices.
 
 
 
• **Gonorrhoea - Treatment and Prevention:**
 
 
• Gonorrhoea is treated with **antibiotics**, typically a combination of ceftriaxone and azithromycin.
 
• Prevention strategies include the use of condoms, regular STD screenings, and limiting the number of sexual partners.
 
• Early detection and treatment are crucial to prevent complications and the spread of the infection.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Burden:** According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, there are approximately **87 million new cases of gonorrhoea** each year globally.
 
• **Antibiotic Resistance:** Gonorrhoea has shown increasing resistance to antibiotics, making it a significant public health concern.
 
• **Co-infections:** Individuals with gonorrhoea are at a higher risk of co-infection with other STDs, including **HIV**.
 
• **Public Health Measures:** Education, awareness campaigns, and accessible healthcare services are essential to reducing the prevalence of gonorrhoea and other STDs.

questions.question: Two resistors of 15 Omega and 5 Omega are connected in series with a 12 V battery. How much current will flow in the circuit?

• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• It is a fundamental law of electrical circuits stating the relationship between **current (I)**, **voltage (V)**, and **resistance (R)**: **V = I × R**.
 
• This law is applicable to **linear circuits** where the resistance remains constant regardless of the voltage or current.
 
 
 
• **Series Circuits:**
 
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance is the **sum of all individual resistances**: **R_total = R1 + R2 + ... + Rn**.
 
• The **current is the same** through all components in a series circuit.
 
• The total voltage is the **sum of the voltages across each component**.

 Total power = **5.4 W + 1.8 W = 7.2 W**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Series Circuits:**

• **Important Note:** If one component in a series circuit fails (e.g., a resistor burns out), the entire circuit becomes open, and **current stops flowing**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resistors in Series vs. Parallel:**

 
 
• In a **series connection**, the total resistance increases as resistors are added.
 
• In a **parallel connection**, the total resistance decreases as resistors are added.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**

questions.question: Archimedes' principle states that when a body is immersed in a fluid, it experiences __________.

options.text: A downward force equal to the weight of fluid displaced by the body
An upward force equal to the weight of the body
An upward force equal to the weight of fluid displaced by the body

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An upward force equal to the weight of fluid displaced by the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Archimedes' Principle:** It states that when a body is fully or partially immersed in a fluid, it experiences an **upward buoyant force** equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it. *Hence, the correct statement is that the body experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the displaced fluid.*
 
• **Buoyant Force:** The upward force exerted by the fluid on the immersed body is termed as the buoyant force. This force acts in the opposite direction of gravity.
 
• **Weight of Displaced Fluid:** The weight of the fluid displaced is calculated as the product of the density of the fluid, the volume of the displaced fluid, and the acceleration due to gravity (**W = ρ × V × g**).
 
• **Equilibrium Condition:** If the buoyant force equals the weight of the body, the body will float. If the weight is greater, the body will sink. If the weight is less, the body will rise until equilibrium is reached.
 
• **Applications:** Archimedes' principle is widely used in shipbuilding, designing submarines, hydrometry, and determining the density of an object by submerging it in a fluid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Archimedes' Principle:** This principle was discovered by the ancient Greek mathematician and physicist, **Archimedes**, around 250 BCE. It is said that he discovered this principle while taking a bath, leading to his famous exclamation, “**Eureka!**”.
 
• **Buoyancy in Fluids:** The principle applies to all fluids, including liquids and gases. For example, helium balloons rise in air because the buoyant force is greater than the weight of the balloon.
 
• **Density and Floating:** Objects with a density less than the fluid float, while those with a higher density sink. For example, ice floats on water because its density is lower than that of water.
 
• **Hydrometer:** The hydrometer, an instrument used to measure the specific gravity of liquids, operates based on Archimedes' principle. It floats higher or lower in a liquid depending on the liquid's density.
 
• **Submarines:** Submarines adjust their buoyancy by filling or emptying ballast tanks with water or air, allowing them to sink, rise, or remain at a specific depth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statement Analysis:**

 
 
• **A downward force equal to the weight of fluid displaced by the body:** This is incorrect. The force due to the fluid is upward, not downward.
 
• **No change in its weight:** Incorrect. The weight of the body remains the same, but the net force acting on the body changes due to the buoyant force.
 
• **An upward force equal to the weight of the body:** Incorrect. The upward force depends on the weight of the displaced fluid, not the weight of the body.
 
• **An upward force equal to the weight of fluid displaced by the body:** Correct. This statement aligns with Archimedes' principle.
 
 
 
• **Practical Examples:**
 
 
• **Ships:** Ships are designed to displace a volume of water equal to their weight, ensuring they float.
 
• **Hot Air Balloons:** They rise because the hot air inside is less dense than the surrounding cooler air, creating buoyant force.
 
• **Floating Icebergs:** Only a small portion of an iceberg is visible above water due to its density being slightly less than seawater.

questions.question: In reproductive health, the aim of contraception is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**to prevent unplanned pregnancies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Contraception** refers to methods or devices used to prevent pregnancy during sexual activity. It allows individuals or couples to plan and control the timing and number of their children.
 
• The primary aim of contraception is **to prevent unplanned pregnancies**, ensuring that families can make informed decisions about parenthood. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Contraception is a significant part of **reproductive health**, promoting physical, emotional, and economic well-being by allowing spacing or limiting the number of children.
 
• It also helps in reducing the **risk of maternal and child mortality**, as planned pregnancies are generally safer for both the mother and child.
 
• Various methods of contraception include **barrier methods** (e.g., condoms), **hormonal methods** (e.g., birth control pills), **intrauterine devices (IUDs)**, and **permanent methods** like sterilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Contraception:**

 
 
• It helps in controlling the **global population growth**, which is crucial for sustainable development and resource management.
 
• Contraception reduces the risk of **sexually transmitted infections (STIs)** like HIV when barrier methods such as condoms are used.
 
• It prevents **teenage pregnancies**, enabling young individuals to complete their education and achieve their career goals.
 
• Family planning through contraception contributes to **gender equality**, as it empowers women to take control of their reproductive health.
 
 
 
• **Popular Contraceptive Methods and Their Features:**
 
 
• **Barrier Methods:** Includes condoms and diaphragms; these are physical devices that block sperm from reaching the egg.
 
• **Hormonal Methods:** Includes oral contraceptive pills, patches, and injections; these regulate hormones to prevent ovulation.
 
• **Intrauterine Devices (IUDs):** T-shaped devices inserted into the uterus to prevent pregnancy; they can be hormonal or copper-based.
 
• **Permanent Methods:** Includes surgical procedures like vasectomy (for males) and tubal ligation (for females) for irreversible contraception.
 
 
 
• **Unplanned Pregnancies:**
 
 
• An unplanned pregnancy occurs when a pregnancy is unintended at the time of conception.
 
• According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, approximately **121 million unintended pregnancies** occur globally each year.
 
• Unplanned pregnancies can result in **health complications**, financial burdens, and emotional stress for individuals or families.
 
 
 
• **Global Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Family Planning 2020 (FP2020)** initiative aims to expand access to contraceptives globally, particularly in developing countries.
 
• The Indian government promotes contraception through its **National Family Planning Programme**, which offers free or subsidized contraceptive methods to the population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "To have more babies" is incorrect as contraception is designed to prevent pregnancy, not facilitate it.
 
• **Option 2:** "To prevent unplanned pregnancies" is correct as the primary purpose of contraception is to allow individuals to plan for pregnancy. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Option 3:** "To make babies healthy" is incorrect as contraception does not directly influence the health of babies; it prevents pregnancies instead.
 
• **Option 4:** "To make twin babies" is incorrect as contraception does not determine the number of babies conceived.
 
 
 
• Contraception is a critical tool in achieving public health goals such as reducing maternal mortality, preventing unsafe abortions, and improving family welfare.

questions.question: What is the effective diameter of the circular outline of a spherical lens called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aperture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **effective diameter** of the circular outline of a spherical lens is called the **aperture**. It determines the amount of light that can pass through the lens.
 
• The aperture of a lens is crucial in controlling the intensity of light entering through the lens and reaching the focal point.
 
• In optical systems, a **larger aperture** allows more light to enter, which is essential for applications like telescopes or cameras where brightness is critical.
 
• The aperture is often represented by a circular boundary or stop that defines the usable portion of the lens for light transmission.
 
• Unlike other parameters like the **focal length** or **radius of curvature**, the aperture directly impacts the field of view and the resolution of the optical system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Optical Centre:**

 
 
• The optical center of a lens is a specific point where light rays pass without deviation.
 
• It is not related to the diameter or size of the lens but is crucial for understanding light behavior in optical systems.
 
• The optical center is used to study how a lens bends light to form images.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length:**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance between the optical center and the focal point where parallel light rays converge or diverge.
 
• It determines the magnification and field of view of the lens.
 
• Unlike the aperture, the focal length is a fixed geometrical property of the lens.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature:**
 
 
• The radius of curvature refers to the radius of the spherical surface of the lens or mirror.
 
• It defines the shape of the lens surface but does not directly influence the amount of light entering the system.
 
• It is essential for calculating the focal length of the lens.
 
 
 
• **Aperture in Practical Applications:**
 
 
• In photography, the aperture is crucial in determining the depth of field and exposure of an image.
 
• In telescopes, a larger aperture improves the resolution and brightness of the observed celestial objects.
 
• In microscopy, the aperture controls the numerical aperture, which influences the resolving power of the microscope.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **aperture** is often confused with the focal length, but they serve different purposes in optics. The aperture controls light intensity, while the focal length determines image magnification and focus.
 
• The **size of the aperture** is usually adjusted using an iris diaphragm in cameras and microscopes.
 
• A **larger aperture** improves brightness but reduces the depth of field, while a **smaller aperture** increases the depth of field but reduces brightness.
 
• The aperture is an integral part of optical systems like cameras, telescopes, and microscopes, influencing image quality and system performance.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is purified by distillation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zinc** is purified by the process of **distillation**, which is a method of separating substances based on differences in their boiling points.
 
• Zinc has a relatively low boiling point of **907°C**, making it suitable for purification by distillation.
 
• During the distillation process, zinc is heated to its boiling point, where it vaporizes. The vapor is then condensed back into a pure liquid or solid form, separating it from impurities.
 
• Other metals like **silver, iron, and copper** are not typically purified by distillation because their boiling points are significantly higher, making this process inefficient or impractical for them.
 
• Distillation is an effective method for purifying metals like zinc, cadmium, and mercury, which have low boiling points and can vaporize easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Silver:**

 
 
• Silver is purified using methods like **electrolytic refining** and **cupellation**.
 
• In electrolytic refining, silver is dissolved in an electrolyte solution, and pure silver is deposited on the cathode.
 
• Silver has a high boiling point of **2162°C**, making distillation impractical for its purification.
 
 
 
• **Iron:**
 
 
• Iron is purified using the **blast furnace** process or by further refining methods like the **Bessemer process**.
 
• Its boiling point is around **2862°C**, far too high for distillation to be used as a purification method.
 
• Methods like reduction and refining are commonly employed to purify iron from its ores.
 
 
 
• **Copper:**
 
 
• Copper is usually purified through **electrolytic refining**.
 
• In this process, impure copper is made the anode, and pure copper is deposited at the cathode.
 
• Copper has a boiling point of **2562°C**, which also makes distillation unsuitable for its purification.
 
 
 
• **Distillation Process:**
 
 
• Distillation is primarily used for metals with **low boiling points**, as it relies on the vaporization and condensation of the metal.
 
• It is commonly used for metals like **zinc, cadmium**, and **mercury** due to their relatively low boiling points.
 
• Impurities with higher boiling points remain as residues, allowing the metal to be purified effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Boiling Points of Metals:**

 
 
• Zinc: **907°C**
 
• Silver: **2162°C**
 
• Iron: **2862°C**
 
• Copper: **2562°C**
 
 
 
• **Suitability of Distillation:**
 
 
• Metals with low boiling points, like zinc, are ideal for distillation-based purification.
 
• High-boiling-point metals require alternative purification methods such as electrolytic refining or reduction.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly explains why gases can be compressed easily compared to solids and liquids?

options.text: Gases have high mass and density
Gases have loosely packed particles with large intermolecular spaces

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gases have loosely packed particles with large intermolecular spaces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Compression of Gases:** Gases can be compressed easily because their particles are **loosely packed** and have large intermolecular spaces. This characteristic allows them to be compressed into smaller volumes by applying pressure.
 
• **Intermolecular Space:** The particles of gases are separated by **large distances** as compared to solids and liquids, which is why they are highly compressible.
 
• **Kinetic Energy:** Gas particles have **high kinetic energy**, which allows them to move freely and occupy any available space. This movement creates significant gaps between particles.
 
• **Absence of Fixed Shape and Volume:** Gases do not have a fixed shape or volume, which makes them easier to compress compared to solids, which are rigid, and liquids, which have fixed volume but no fixed shape.
 
• **Applications:** The compressibility of gases is utilized in various applications, such as in **compressed gas cylinders** used in industries, medical oxygen tanks, and LPG cylinders for domestic purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Gases:**

 
 
• Gases have no definite shape or volume and take the shape of their container.
 
• The particles in gases are in constant random motion, colliding with each other and the walls of the container.
 
• The compressibility of gases is due to the large amount of empty space between particles.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Solids and Liquids:**
 
 
• **Solids:** Particles are tightly packed, with very little space between them, making them incompressible.
 
• **Liquids:** Particles are closer than in gases but not as tightly packed as in solids. Liquids are slightly compressible, but the effect is negligible compared to gases.
 
 
 
• **Boyle's Law:**
 
 
• Boyle's Law states that the **pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume** at a constant temperature.
 
• This principle demonstrates the compressibility of gases, as increasing pressure decreases the volume of gas due to reduced space between particles.
 
 
 
• **Real-World Applications:**
 
 
• Compressed gases are used in industries for operations such as welding and cutting.
 
• Medical oxygen cylinders are compressed to store large amounts of oxygen in portable containers.
 
• Refrigerators and air conditioners use compressed gases in their cooling systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** Gases do not have low kinetic energy. In fact, they have high kinetic energy, which allows their particles to move freely. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Option 2:** Gases have low mass and density compared to solids and liquids, but this does not explain their compressibility. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Option 3:** Gases occupy space and have volume, even though they lack a fixed shape. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Option 4:** The correct explanation is that gases have loosely packed particles with large intermolecular spaces, which makes them compressible. *Hence, this option is correct.*

questions.question: In the context of carbon compounds, what characterises a 'branched chain' structure?

options.text: Carbon atoms are bonded to four different atoms.
Carbon atoms are arranged in a continuous, straight line.
Carbon atoms form a closed ring structure.
Carbon atoms are attached to the main carbon chain, forming side groups.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon atoms are attached to the main carbon chain, forming side groups.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a **branched-chain structure**, carbon atoms are arranged such that some carbon atoms are attached to the main carbon chain as side groups.
 
• The main chain refers to the longest continuous sequence of carbon atoms, while the side chains or branches consist of smaller carbon groups attached to the primary chain.
 
• These branches are often referred to as alkyl groups (e.g., methyl, ethyl), which are formed by the removal of one hydrogen atom from an alkane.
 
• This structural arrangement leads to **isomerism** in organic compounds, where compounds with the same molecular formula have different structural arrangements.
 
• Branched chains impact the **physical and chemical properties** of compounds, such as boiling points and reactivity, due to differences in molecular geometry and intermolecular forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Branched Carbon Chains:**

 
 
• Branched chains are **non-linear structures** formed by carbon atoms.
 
• They exhibit lower boiling points compared to straight-chain structures of the same molecular formula due to weaker **van der Waals forces**.
 
• Branched hydrocarbons are often less dense and more volatile than their straight-chain counterparts.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Structures:**
 
 
• **Straight Chain:** Carbon atoms are arranged in a continuous, linear sequence (e.g., n-butane).
 
• **Cyclic Structures:** Carbon atoms form a closed ring, such as in cycloalkanes (e.g., cyclohexane).
 
 
 
• **Examples of Branched Compounds:**
 
 
• **Isobutane:** A branched isomer of butane with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀.
 
• **2-Methylpropane:** An example of a branched-chain alkane derived from propane.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism in Organic Chemistry:**
 
 
• Structural isomerism occurs when compounds with the same molecular formula differ in their bonding arrangements.
 
• Branched isomers often display unique chemical and physical properties compared to their straight-chain counterparts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. Carbon atoms bonded to four different atoms refer to a **chiral center**, not a branched chain.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect. A continuous, straight line refers to a **straight-chain structure**, not a branched one.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect. A closed ring structure describes **cyclic compounds**, not branched chains.
 
• **Option 4:** Correct. Branched chains are characterized by carbon atoms attached as side groups to the main carbon chain.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic property of a material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistivity** is a **characteristic property of a material** as it depends solely on the material and not on its shape or size.
 
• It is defined as the **inherent opposition** of a material to the flow of electric current. The formula for resistivity is: **ρ = R × A / L**, where:
 
 
• ρ is the resistivity of the material.
 
• R is the resistance.
 
• A is the cross-sectional area.
 
• L is the length of the conductor.
 
 
 
• Unlike resistance, which depends on the material's dimensions, resistivity is a **fixed property** for a specific material at a given temperature.
 
• Resistivity is measured in **ohm-meters (Ω·m)** in the SI system.
 
• It is used to classify materials as **conductors** (low resistivity), **semiconductors** (moderate resistivity), and **insulators** (high resistivity).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Resistance:**

 
 
• Resistance is the measure of how much a material opposes the flow of electric current. It depends on the material's **resistivity**, its dimensions (length and cross-sectional area), and the temperature.
 
• The formula for resistance is **R = ρ × L / A**, where ρ is resistivity, L is length, and A is cross-sectional area.
 
• Resistance is measured in **ohms (Ω)**.
 
 
 
• **Voltage:**
 
 
• Voltage is the **electric potential difference** between two points. It is the driving force that pushes current through a circuit.
 
• It is measured in **volts (V)**.
 
• Voltage depends on the power supply or source and not on the material's properties.
 
 
 
• **Current:**
 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor. It is measured in **amperes (A)**.
 
• It depends on the **voltage** across the conductor and the **resistance** of the material, as described by Ohm's Law: **I = V / R**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistivity:**
 
 
• Resistivity is used in designing electrical components like **resistors** and **heating elements**.
 
• It helps in selecting materials for specific applications (e.g., copper for wires due to low resistivity, rubber for insulation due to high resistivity).
 
• Resistivity measurements are also used in **geophysics** to identify different types of rocks and minerals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Dependence:**

 
 
• Resistivity of most materials **increases with temperature** (e.g., metals).
 
• In semiconductors, resistivity **decreases with temperature**, making them useful for temperature sensors.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Materials and Resistivity:**
 
 
• **Silver:** Lowest resistivity among metals (highly conductive).
 
• **Rubber:** High resistivity (excellent insulator).
 
• **Silicon:** Moderate resistivity (semiconductor).
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:** The relationship between voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) is given by **V = I × R**.

questions.question: Why does growth in plants occur only in specific regions?

options.text: Water reaches only the upper parts of the plant.
Gravity prevents growth in certain regions.
Only some parts of the plant receive sunlight.
Meristematic tissue is located only in specific regions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meristematic tissue is located only in specific regions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Plant growth occurs in specific regions because of the presence of **meristematic tissue**. These tissues are undifferentiated and actively divide to contribute to the growth of the plant.
 
• **Meristematic tissues** are located in certain areas such as the tips of roots and shoots (apical meristems), the circumference of stems and roots (lateral meristems), and certain areas of leaves (intercalary meristems).

Consider a ray of light travelling obliquely from air into a glass slab. Which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

(i) The angle of incidence is smaller than the angle of refraction.

(ii) The angle of incidence is greater than the angle of emergence.

(iii) The speed of light decreases as the light ray enters from air to glass.

(iv) The incident ray and the emergent ray are parallel to each other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (iii) and (iv)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Statement (i): "The angle of incidence is smaller than the angle of refraction." - When light passes from air (less dense medium) to glass (denser medium), it bends towards the normal. - The angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence. - **Thus, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• Statement (ii): "The angle of incidence is greater than the angle of emergence." - For a glass slab, the angle of incidence and the angle of emergence are always equal because the ray of light emerges parallel to the incident ray after refraction. - **Thus, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• Statement (iii): "The speed of light decreases as the light ray enters from air to glass." - Light travels faster in air than in glass due to the difference in the optical density of the two mediums. - The refractive index (n) of glass is higher than that of air, causing the speed of light to decrease in the glass medium. - **This statement is correct.**
 
• Statement (iv): "The incident ray and the emergent ray are parallel to each other." - In a glass slab, the light ray undergoes two refractions: first when entering the glass and second when exiting it. - The incident ray and emergent ray are parallel to each other because the lateral displacement of the light ray occurs within the slab, but the overall direction remains unchanged. - **This statement is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Refraction of Light:**

 
 
• Refraction is the phenomenon where light changes its direction as it passes from one medium to another due to a change in its speed.
 
• The amount of bending depends on the refractive index of the two media involved.
 
• The Snell's Law formula is: n₁ sin(θ₁) = n₂ sin(θ₂), where n₁ and n₂ are the refractive indices, and θ₁ and θ₂ are the angles of incidence and refraction.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:**
 
 
• The refractive index (n) is a measure of how much the speed of light decreases in a given medium. For example: - Air: n ≈ 1 - Glass: n ≈ 1.5
 
• A higher refractive index indicates a denser medium and a greater bending of light.
 
 
 
• **Lateral Displacement in a Glass Slab:**
 
 
• When a light ray passes through a parallel-sided glass slab, the emergent ray is displaced laterally but remains parallel to the incident ray.
 
• The lateral displacement depends on: - Thickness of the slab - Angle of incidence - Refractive index of the medium
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refraction:**
 
 
• Used in lenses to focus or disperse light (e.g., eyeglasses, cameras, microscopes).
 
• Explains natural phenomena such as the formation of rainbows and mirages.
 
• Essential in optical instruments like prisms and spectrometers.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true according to Thomson's Model of Atom?

options.text: Electrons are concentrated in the nucleus.
Electrons are fixed in the orbits.
Electrons are spread randomly in a positively charged sphere.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrons are spread randomly in a positively charged sphere.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomson's Model of Atom** (proposed by **J.J. Thomson in 1904**) is often referred to as the "Plum Pudding Model" or "Watermelon Model."
 
• According to this model, an atom consists of a **positively charged sphere** in which **electrons are embedded randomly**, similar to seeds in a watermelon.
 
• Thomson proposed that the **positive charge** is uniformly distributed across the sphere, and the negatively charged electrons are scattered within it, ensuring an overall **neutral charge of the atom**.
 
• The correct statement from the options given is "Electrons are spread randomly in a positively charged sphere__" as this is the key feature of Thomson's model.
 
• This model was significant as it was the **first scientific attempt** to describe the structure of an atom, even though it was later disproved by **Ernest Rutherford's gold foil experiment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of Thomson's Model:**

 
 
• The atom is a **neutral entity**, meaning the total positive charge is equal to the total negative charge.
 
• Electrons (**negatively charged particles**) are embedded within a sphere of **positive charge**, like "plums in a pudding."
 
• The atom's mass is primarily concentrated within the positively charged sphere.
 
• This model did not explain the arrangement of electrons or the stability of atoms during chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Disproval of Thomson's Model:**
 
 
• In 1911, **Ernest Rutherford** conducted the **gold foil experiment**, which revealed that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at their center, leading to the development of the **Rutherford Model of the Atom**.
 
• Thomson's model failed to explain the **scattering of alpha particles** observed in Rutherford's experiment.
 
 
 
• **Other Atomic Models:**
 
 
• **Rutherford's Nuclear Model:** Proposed the existence of a nucleus, with electrons revolving around it in circular orbits.
 
• **Bohr's Model:** Improved Rutherford's model by introducing quantized orbits for electrons to explain atomic stability and spectral lines.
 
• **Quantum Mechanical Model:** The modern model of the atom based on the principles of quantum mechanics, describing electron behavior as a probability distribution.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Thomson's Discovery:**
 
 
• The discovery of electrons paved the way for understanding **electricity, magnetism, and chemical bonding**.
 
• The identification of subatomic particles laid the foundation for **modern physics and chemistry**.
 
• Thomson's work earned him the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1906** for his discovery of the electron.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statement Analysis:**

 
 
• Statement 1: "Electrons are concentrated in the nucleus" – Incorrect. Electrons are not located in the nucleus; the nucleus contains protons and neutrons.
 
• Statement 2: "Electrons are attached to neutrons" – Incorrect. Electrons are negatively charged particles and are not attached to neutrons, which are neutral.
 
• Statement 3: "Electrons are fixed in the orbits" – Incorrect. This concept belongs to **Bohr's atomic model**, not Thomson's model.
 
• Statement 4: "Electrons are spread randomly in a positively charged sphere" – Correct. This is the core idea of Thomson's model.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:** Thomson's model was proposed in **1904**, and it was a significant step in understanding atomic structure, despite its limitations.
 
• **Scientific Contributions:** J.J. Thomson's discovery of the electron revolutionized the field of physics and chemistry, providing insights into the nature of matter.

__
 
• **Assertion: Sound waves are non-mechanical waves.**

 
 
• This statement is **false**. Sound waves are, in fact, mechanical waves because they require a medium (such as air, water, or a solid) to propagate. They transfer energy through the vibration of particles in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Reason: Sound waves require a material medium for their propagation.**
 
 
• This statement is **true**. Sound waves cannot travel through a vacuum because they depend on the vibration of particles in a material medium to propagate.
 
 
 
• The correct explanation lies in the nature of sound waves. They are longitudinal mechanical waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• Examples of sound wave transmission include:
 
 
• Sound traveling through air (e.g., human speech).
 
• Sound traveling through water (e.g., sonar technology).
 
• Sound traveling through solids (e.g., vibrations in a metal rod).
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:** Since the assertion claims that sound waves are non-mechanical (incorrect), and the reason correctly states that sound waves require a material medium, the answer is **"Assertion is false but reason is true."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Sound Waves:**

 
 
• Sound waves are **longitudinal waves**, meaning the particle displacement is parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• They are **mechanical waves**, requiring a material medium (air, water, or solid) to travel.
 
• Sound cannot travel in a **vacuum** because there are no particles to transmit the vibrations.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the medium's properties. For instance:
 
 
• In air at 20°C, the speed of sound is approximately **343 m/s**.
 
• In water, it is around **1482 m/s**.
 
• In solids like steel, it can reach up to **5000 m/s**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Types of Mechanical Waves:**
 
 
• **Longitudinal Waves:** Particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the wave's direction of travel. Examples: Sound waves, seismic P-waves.
 
• **Transverse Waves:** Particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the wave's direction of travel. Examples: Water waves, light waves (electromagnetic, non-mechanical).
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Mechanical and Non-Mechanical Waves:**
 
 
• **Mechanical Waves:** Require a material medium for propagation (e.g., sound, water waves).
 
• **Non-Mechanical Waves:** Do not require a medium and can propagate through a vacuum (e.g., electromagnetic waves like light, radio waves).
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sound Waves:**
 
 
• **Ultrasound:** Used in medical imaging and diagnostics.
 
• **Sonar:** Used in submarines and underwater navigation.
 
• **Communication:** Human speech and various audio technologies like telephones and speakers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Speed of Sound in Different Media:**

 
 
• Sound travels faster in solids than in liquids, and faster in liquids than in gases due to the closer particle arrangement in solids.
 
 
 
• **Echo:** The reflection of sound waves from a surface back to the listener. Used in echolocation by animals like bats and dolphins.
 
• **Noise vs. Music:** Sound waves can be categorized based on their regularity:

A water tank is (5)/(8) full. If 12 buckets of water are taken out and 9 buckets of water are poured into it, the water tank would be (7)/(12) full.

**Given:**

A water tank is (5)/(8) full.

12 buckets of water are taken out and 9 buckets of water are poured into it.

After this, the tank is (7)/(12) full.

Find the total capacity of the tank in buckets.

**Formula used:**

Capacity of the tank = Total number of buckets when full.

Change in water level = Difference in fraction values × Total capacity.

**Calculations:**

Initial water in tank = (5)/(8) of total capacity.

Final water in tank = (7)/(12) of total capacity.

Change in water level = Water removed + Water added.

⇒ |(5)/(8) - (7)/(12)| × Total capacity = 12 - 9.

⇒ Difference in fractions = LCM of denominators (8, 12) = 24.

⇒ (5)/(8) = (15)/(24) and (7)/(12) = (14)/(24).

⇒ Difference = |15 - 14| / 24 = (1)/(24).

Change in water = Total capacity × (1)/(24).

⇒ Total capacity × (1)/(24) = 12 - 9 = 3.

⇒ Total capacity = 3 × 24 = 72 buckets.

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 4 days. B alone can do the same work in 8 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B working together can complete the work in 4 days.

B alone can complete the work in 8 days.

**Formula used:**

Total work = LCM of individual times

Efficiency = Total work ÷ Time

Time taken by A alone to complete double the work = (2 × Total work) ÷ Efficiency of A

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Calculate Total Work

Total work = LCM of 4 and 8 = 8 units

Step 2: Calculate Efficiency

Efficiency of A and B together = Total work ÷ Time = 8 ÷ 4 = 2 units/day

Efficiency of B = Total work ÷ Time = 8 ÷ 8 = 1 unit/day

Efficiency of A = Efficiency of A and B together - Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 2 - 1 = 1 unit/day

Step 3: Time taken by A alone to do double the work

Double the work = 2 × Total work = 2 × 8 = 16 units

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency = 16 ÷ 1

⇒ Time = 16 days

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**
